processes: Fixing which element an atom is
plainLanguageExplanation: A proton is one of the three particles that make up atoms, and it is the one that gives an atom its identity. A proton is a tiny particle with a positive electric charge, living in the nucleus — the dense core at the center of every atom. The most important fact about protons is this: the NUMBER of protons decides what element an atom is. Every atom with exactly 6 protons is carbon. Every atom with 79 protons is gold. There is no way around it — change the proton count and you change the element. That is why the atomic number on the periodic table is just the proton count. Protons also do the pulling in an atom: their positive charge attracts the negative electrons, keeping the electron cloud wrapped around the nucleus. Without protons, there would be no elements, no atoms, no chemistry — protons are the identity of everything around you.

keyFacts.label: Charge
keyFacts.value: Positive — one proton has a +1 charge

keyFacts.label: Location
keyFacts.value: In the nucleus, the dense core of the atom

keyFacts.label: The key job
keyFacts.value: Its count defines the element — 6 protons = carbon, 79 protons = gold

keyFacts.label: Atomic number
keyFacts.value: The periodic table's atomic number is the proton count

keyFacts.label: Pulling power
keyFacts.value: Attracts negative electrons, holding the atom together

keyFacts.label: Mass
keyFacts.value: Heavy — about 1,836 times more massive than an electron

whyItMatters: Protons are the identity of matter. The entire periodic table is a list of proton counts, and every element on it is what it is because of how many protons it carries. Understanding protons unlocks why elements differ, why the table is ordered the way it is, and why atoms behave the way they do.
tagline: The particle that names the element
didYouKnow: If you changed just ONE proton in a carbon atom, you would turn it into nitrogen — the element next door on the periodic table. Proton count is everything.
compareReason: The proton and neutron are inseparable neighbors in the nucleus, yet one carries the element's identity and the other carries nothing — comparing them makes the proton's defining role unforgettable.
